title_en: Cheng Guoyi, Wang Jinyuan, Gu Jinsheng, and Wang Hengmao — dereliction of duty case
keywords_en: criminal; dereliction of duty; second instance; High People's Court; Shanxi Province; state organ; criminal law; elements of the crime of dereliction of duty; appropriateness of sentencing; affirm the original judgment; imported equipment; fire accident; lack of safety precautions
full_text_en:
Cheng Guoyi, Wang Jinyuan, Gu Jinsheng, and Wang Hengmao — crime of dereliction of duty

Defendant: Cheng Guoyi, male, 33 years old, formerly Deputy Mine Director of the Fanshigou Coal Mine, Gujiao District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.

Defendant: Wang Jinyuan, male, 55 years old, formerly Secretary of the General Party Branch of the Fanshigou Coal Mine, Gujiao District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.

Defendant: Gu Jinsheng, male, 49 years old, formerly Deputy Director of the Taiyuan City Coal Administration Bureau, Shanxi Province.

Defendant: Wang Hengmao, male, 52 years old, formerly Deputy District Head of Gujiao District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.

The above-named defendants were all arrested on May 29, 1986.

The defendants Cheng Guoyi, Wang Jinyuan, Gu Jinsheng, and Wang Hengmao were indicted by the Taiyuan City People's Procuratorate, Shanxi Province, before the Taiyuan City Intermediate People's Court on charges of dereliction of duty. The Taiyuan City Intermediate People's Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and conducted a public trial on August 30, 1986. The following facts were found upon trial:

In October 1984, the former Shanxi Provincial Local Coal Industry Administration Bureau arranged for the Fanshigou Coal Mine in Gujiao District, Taiyuan City, to import a set of Mark 22 thin-seam coal mining machinery from the United States. After negotiating and signing the contract with the U.S. party, the Provincial Coal Administration Bureau, in January and March 1985, respectively organized Wang Jinyuan, Cheng Guoyi, Gu Jinsheng, Wang Hengmao, and others to travel to the United States for training and intermediary inspection. After the personnel returned to China, the Provincial Coal Administration Bureau held a work meeting on May 30 and 31 of the same year to report on the overseas delegation and the unpacking and acceptance inspection of the machinery. It was determined that Cheng Guoyi, Gu Jinsheng, and Wang Hengmao would be the project leaders responsible for the imported machinery.

From November 1985 to January 1986, the imported machinery from the United States arrived at the Fanshigou Mine in three separate shipments. Except for two large crates placed at the pithead, the remaining 45 crates and 68 items were all stacked in the yard of the mine's mechanical repair workshop without any protection. They were not covered with tarpaulins until February 21, 1986. In the yard where the imported machinery was stored, there were no fire prevention signs, no safety precautions, and many people came and went. Management was chaotic, and the machinery was left without dedicated supervision for a period of three months. This eventually led to a major fire on March 3, 1986, caused by workers Kang Ping and Zhai Bugao (separately prosecuted), who smoked and played cards on the crates of the imported machinery and left behind ignition sources that ignited sawdust on the ground beneath the crates. The fire destroyed most of the machinery, causing direct economic losses of over RMB 2.6 million and rendering the nearly RMB 6 million machinery set unusable as a complete unit.

The trial court, the Taiyuan City Intermediate People's Court, found: The defendant Cheng Guoyi, as Deputy Mine Director, a member of the machinery acceptance and commissioning leadership group, and a project leader for the imported machinery, directly participated in the negotiations for the import and the internship in the United States. Before the machinery arrived at the mine, the Party branch meeting explicitly assigned Cheng to focus on the machinery work, and he was informed by the Provincial Commodity Inspection Bureau of precautions including the prohibition of smoking in the machinery acceptance area. After the machinery arrived at the mine, the head of the Mine's Mechanical and Electrical Section, Zhang Shiwu, submitted a written proposal to Cheng suggesting that the mine leadership study and adopt necessary protective measures for the machinery already on site. None of these matters prompted Cheng Guoyi to take the matter seriously or to adopt safety precautions. The defendant Wang Jinyuan, as Secretary of the Mine's General Party Branch, was presiding over the mine's overall work at the time and was designated as Deputy Head of the imported machinery acceptance and commissioning leadership group. He had also participated in the internship in the United States. After the imported machinery arrived at the mine, he neither convened meetings to study safety precautions nor educated the workers on safety. The defendant Gu Jinsheng, as Deputy Director of the Taiyuan City Coal Administration Bureau in charge of production technology, personally participated in the negotiations for the imported machinery and led a team to the United States as the head of the intermediary inspection group. After returning to China, Gu was designated as a project leader for the imported machinery. However, Gu neither supervised nor inspected the safety precautions for the storage of the machinery. In February 1986, when the mine studied the acceptance work of the machinery, he did not even go to the site to inspect. The defendant Wang Hengmao, as Deputy District Head in charge of industry in the district government, participated in the intermediary inspection trip to the United States. After returning to China, Wang was designated as a project leader for the imported machinery. However, from the time the machinery arrived at the mine until it was burned, Wang never made any specific safety requirements, nor did he conduct any on-site inspections. The defendants Cheng Guoyi, Wang Jinyuan, Gu Jinsheng, and Wang Hengmao, as state personnel, adopted an extremely irresponsible attitude towards the storage, custody, and safety precautions of the coal mining machinery imported at great expense, leading to the major fire disaster that destroyed most of the machinery, causing heavy losses to public property. Their conduct constituted the crime of dereliction of duty as stipulated in Article 187 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

On September 1, 1986, the Taiyuan City Intermediate People's Court, for the crime of dereliction of duty, sentenced defendant Cheng Guoyi to four years' imprisonment, Wang Jinyuan to two years' imprisonment, and Gu Jinsheng and Wang Hengmao each to one year's imprisonment.

The defendants Cheng Guoyi, Wang Jinyuan, Gu Jinsheng, and Wang Hengmao appealed separately to the Shanxi Province High People's Court, claiming that the facts established in the first-instance judgment did not match the actual circumstances and that the sentences were excessive.

Upon second-instance trial, the Shanxi Province High People's Court held: The appellants Cheng Guoyi, Wang Jinyuan, Gu Jinsheng, and Wang Hengmao, as state personnel, adopted an extremely irresponsible attitude towards the storage, custody, and safety precautions of the machinery imported at great expense, leading to the major fire disaster that destroyed most of the machinery, causing heavy losses to state property. Their conduct constituted the crime of dereliction of duty. The facts found in the original judgment were clear, the conviction was accurate, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. The grounds of appeal raised by Cheng Guoyi, Wang Jinyuan, Gu Jinsheng, and Wang Hengmao were untenable. Pursuant to Article 136, Item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on September 16, 1986, the court ruled to dismiss the appeals and affirm the original judgment.
